# Identity / polyrob / local profile

One line per setting: NAME — default — meaning. Code anchors and full prose:
`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. Index: `references/configuration.md`.

- POLYROB_LOCAL — default: OFF — Single-user terminal profile; flips the `_SAFE_LOCAL_FLAGS` group ON as a default.
- POLYROB_DATA_DIR — default: unset — Isolation switch (doc 01/06): when set — the headless/server case — the runtime data home (goals.db/cron.db/memory.db + agent workspaces) lives THERE, OUTSIDE the code tree, and the workspace is under it (not cwd).
- POLYROB_PROJECT_DIR — default: unset — When set, the agent uses this folder as ONE persistent workspace shared across sessions/goals/cron (Claude-Code style), **independent** of `POLYROB_DATA_DIR`.
- POLYROB_LOG_DIR — default: unset — Runtime log directory override.
- POLYROB_PROJECT_SECRET_REFUSE — default: 0 — When truthy, refuse to start if the cwd-default persistent workspace contains secrets/`.git` (SEC-1).
- POLYROB_REQUIRE_PAIRING — default: OFF — Owner-allowlist + DM-pairing ingress gate; when ON, an unpaired sender or unreadable pairing store is denied at the surface dispatcher; unused pairing codes expire after 15 minutes.
- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — default: unset — Telegram bot token (from @BotFather) for the `polyrob telegram` local-polling surface.
- ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS — default: unset — Comma list of raw Telegram numeric user ids allowed to drive the bot.
- POLYROB_OWNER_TELEGRAM_ID — default: unset — The owner's raw Telegram numeric id, used for two things: (1) the **inbound owner alias** — an inbound from this id is aliased to the OWNER principal (`POLYROB_OWNER_USER_ID`) instead of its surface-hashed `u_…` id, so the owner's chat sha…
- POLYROB_OWNER_EMAIL — default: unset — The owner's email address for **out-of-band cron delivery** (`deliver="email"`) on single-owner headless deploys where no `user_directory` service is registered.
- OWNER_SURFACE — default: unset (= telegram) — the owner-notice fan-out order for `deliver_user_message` (approvals, credit sentinel, goal-blocked, settlement, cron reports) — a comma list of surface ids, primary first (e.g. `slack,telegram`).
- OWNER_<SURFACE>_ID — default: unset — The owner's address on that surface for the `OWNER_SURFACE` fan-out (mirrors `POLYROB_OWNER_TELEGRAM_ID`/`POLYROB_OWNER_EMAIL`, which telegram/email keep using). `SURFACE` is the surface catalog's `owner_env`: `SLACK`, `DISCORD`, `SIGNAL`,…
- SINGULAR_CHAT_ENABLED — default: OFF (**ON for every polyrob <surface> daemon and polyrob gateway**) — Installs the outbound surface bus so agent replies route to a chat surface.
- <SURFACE>_SURFACE_ENABLED — default: **configured = on** for a catalog row with auto_start (every new surface); OFF otherwise; **ON for polyrob <surface>** (each surface daemon sets its own flag) — Per-surface override for `polyrob gateway`: unset → a surface starts when its required credentials are set; `false` keeps it off; `true` forces it on.
- GROUP_DEFAULT_MODE — default: mention — the default `chat.mode` for a room with no per-chat overlay.
- GROUP_TURN_TOOLS — default: task,web_fetch,defi_data — the read-only toolset of EVERY room-bound (public) session, owner included.
- GROUP_REPLY_CAP_PER_HOUR — default: 20 — max committed replies `MessageRouter.publish` sends into one room chat per rolling hour; over cap the reply is suppressed (logged, never queued) and never counted twice.
- GROUP_MEMBER_COOLDOWN_SEC — default: 20 — minimum seconds between two triggers from the SAME sender (human or bot) in one room chat; a trigger inside the window is refused (`route_inbound` DENIED, silent).
- GROUP_BOT_LOOP_MAX — default: 20 — max bot-authored triggers allowed in one room chat within `GROUP_BOT_LOOP_WINDOW_SEC`; the limit-th+ trip records a `bot_loop_trip` and every further bot trigger is refused until `GROUP_BOT_LOOP_COOLDOWN_SEC` elapses.
- GROUP_BOT_LOOP_WINDOW_SEC — default: 300 — the rolling window `GROUP_BOT_LOOP_MAX` counts bot triggers over.
- GROUP_BOT_LOOP_COOLDOWN_SEC — default: 600 — once the bot-loop guard trips, how long every bot trigger in that room chat is refused before the guard re-arms.
- GROUP_LEDGER_MAX_ROWS_PER_CHAT — default: 2000 — max rows `group_ledger` retains per `(surface, chat_id)`; on every `append` the oldest rows beyond this count are deleted (newest kept).
- GROUP_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS — default: 14 — wall-clock age window `group_ledger` retains per chat; a row older than `time.time() - GROUP_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS*86400` is deleted on the next `append` (prune-on-append) and cannot be read back even without one, since `tail` also prunes…
- VOICE_TRANSCRIPTION_ENABLED — default: ON — Transcribe inbound voice/audio to text before routing (#9), so a voice note is handled like a typed message.
- VOICE_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL — default: base — faster-whisper model size (`tiny`/`base`/`small`/`medium`/`large-v3`).
- OWNER_THREAD_INJECT — default: ON — read the thread INTO sessions — the tail on an owner session's first turn, the delta (other sessions/rails) on every later turn and mid-run drain, the referent of a Telegram quote-reply, the rail slice for an autonomous run.
- OWNER_THREAD_TAIL_HOURS — default: 24 — the tail window a fresh owner session is shown (whichever of hours/rows is smaller; the block is capped at 6000 chars, owner comments and agent replies first, every other row one short line).
- OWNER_THREAD_TAIL_ROWS — default: 40 — the tail row cap.
- CORRESPONDENT_REQUIRE_APPROVAL — default: ON (True) (OFF under AUTONOMY_MODE=autonomous) — A newly auto-seeded correspondent is PENDING (owner must `polyrob owner approve`) before replies route.
- CORRESPONDENT_MAX_NEW_PER_DAY — default: 20 — Per-tenant cap on new correspondents seeded per 24h (bounds injected mass-contact).
- OUTBOUND_POLICY — default: allowlist (open under AUTONOMY_MODE=autonomous) — pure outbound-policy model (`open|domains|allowlist|off` ladder). `resolve_outbound_policy` merges env-or-mode-default with an optional guarded `outbound.policy` pref via the `stricter_policy` merge kind (pref can only TIGHTEN, never loose…
- OUTBOUND_DOMAINS — default: unset (empty) — Comma-separated domain allowlist consulted when `OUTBOUND_POLICY=domains` (email-shaped targets only; other surfaces fall back to the exact-address allowlist).
- OUTBOUND_DAILY_SEND_CAP — default: 30 — Control-plane cap on outbound sends/day once policy is `open`/`domains` (mirrors the `USER_DELIVERY_DAILY_CAP` convention).
- CORRESPONDENT_TTL_DAYS — default: 0 (never) — Days of inactivity before a correspondent binding is removed (stops resolving; the next outbound to that contact seeds it again). `0` = never — expiry silently breaks reply routing for long-quiet contacts, so it is an explicit opt-in.
- CORRESPONDENT_REPLY_MAX_ROUNDS — default: 5 — Outbound messages per correspondent per 24h allowed under the scoped tainted-reply exemption (counted from the ConversationStore).
- MAX_EPHEMERAL_MESSAGES — default: 30 — Cap on the one-shot ephemeral injection queue (correspondent replies / recall notes); overflow drops the OLDEST with a WARN.
- DEAD_TARGET_REGISTRY — default: true — Skip outbound sends to provably-dead targets (bot blocked / chat deleted), auto-revive on inbound from the target.
- EMAIL_IMAP_POLL_SEC — default: 60 — Seconds between IMAP polls for new mail (no IDLE in v1).
- EMAIL_AUTONOMY_RUNTIME — default: OFF — Whether `polyrob email` starts the shared autonomy runtime (goal dispatcher + cron ticker + curator + surface GC).
- API_AUTONOMY_RUNTIME — default: **ON** — Whether the api process (`polyrob serve`) starts the shared autonomy loops.
- GMAIL_EMAIL / GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD — default: unset — Mail credentials for the `email` tool (SMTP send + IMAP read) — the email surface reuses the same tool/creds.
- GMAIL_IMAP_SERVER / GMAIL_SMTP_SERVER / GMAIL_SMTP_PORT — default: imap.gmail.com / smtp.gmail.com / 587 — IMAP/SMTP server endpoints for the email tool; point these at any provider.
- EMAIL_PROVIDER — default: auto — Which transport backs the agent's email: `smtp` | `agentmail`.
- AGENTMAIL_API_KEY — default: unset — AgentMail (api.agentmail.to) API key.
- POLYROB_AGENT_EMAIL — default: unset — Explicit override for the agent's OWN sender address (distinct from `POLYROB_OWNER_EMAIL`, an outbound target).
- WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN — default: unset — Meta permanent/system-user access token used by the Cloud API sender client.
- WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID — default: unset — Meta Phone Number ID of the sending number.
- WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN — default: unset — Token echoed back on the GET webhook verify handshake (Meta webhook setup).
- WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET — default: unset — HMAC-SHA256 payload-signature secret (Meta app secret). **Unset ⇒ inbound webhook payloads are rejected** (fail-closed).
- WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME — default: task_ready — Approved utility template used to re-open the 24h messaging window for a proactive (agent-initiated) message.
- FEISHU_APP_ID / FEISHU_APP_SECRET — default: unset (secret, masked) — Feishu / Lark surface credentials: the custom app's App ID (`cli_…`) + App Secret.
- FEISHU_DOMAIN — default: lark — Which Open-API host the Feishu surface uses: `lark` (open.larksuite.com, international — the default: it needs no mainland-verified entity) or `feishu` (open.feishu.cn, mainland).
- FEISHU_TRANSPORT — default: ws — How Feishu / Lark events arrive: `ws` (the lark-oapi long connection, no public URL, needs the `[feishu]` extra) or `webhook` (the event request URL `https://<host>/webhooks/feishu` on the gateway's shared webhook server — bare install; ne…
- FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY / FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN — default: unset (secret, masked) — The Feishu app's Event Subscription secrets for `FEISHU_TRANSPORT=webhook`.
- FEISHU_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_UNSIGNED — default: **OFF** — Opt-in for Feishu webhook mode with only `FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN` and no `FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY`.
- DINGTALK_CLIENT_ID / DINGTALK_CLIENT_SECRET — default: unset (secret, masked) — DingTalk surface credentials: the internal app's Client ID (AppKey, also its robotCode) + Client Secret (AppSecret).
- SLACK_BOT_TOKEN / SLACK_APP_TOKEN — default: unset (secret, masked) — Slack surface credentials: bot token (`xoxb-`) + Socket-Mode app token (`xapp-`); both required or `polyrob slack` refuses to start.
- DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN — default: unset (secret, masked) — Discord surface bot token (a `--token` CLI option wins over the env).
- SIGNAL_DAEMON_URL — default: http://127.0.0.1:8080 — Base URL of the local `signal-cli daemon --http` the Signal surface talks to.
- SIGNAL_ACCOUNT — default: unset — The Signal account (+E164 number) the surface sends/receives as; required for `polyrob signal`.
- TWITTER_BOT_USER_ID — default: unset — The bot's own X numeric user id for the X DM surface; unset = discovered via `get_me()` at startup (one API call saved when set).
- TWITTER_BOT_USERNAME — default: unset — The bot's own X handle (without `@`), shown beside the X API line of the identity status section; unset = the handle is omitted.
- WEBHOOK_PATH — default: /telegram/webhook — URL path for the Telegram webhook mode (explicitly not the old bot's hardcoded `/mvpbot`).
- TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME — default: unset — the bot's @username without '@', used for room mention detection when getMe is unavailable at boot; getMe still wins when it succeeds.
- DEV_RAIL_SCRIPT — default: unset (a default path in the install tree) — Absolute path to the Telegram `/dev` rail's inject script.
- CHAT_INTENT_CLASSIFIER — default: OFF — Enable the chat-surface intent classifier (pre-routing intent detection on inbound chat messages).
- OUTBOUND_QUEUE_ENABLED — default: OFF — Durable outbound send queue (retry + dead-letter) behind `publish()`'s PRIMARY reply routing (direct-send vs. queued-with-retry for a locally-subscribed surface); OFF = direct legacy sends.
- VOICE_TRANSCRIPTION_REQUIRED — default: OFF — Make a missing faster-whisper engine a startup ERROR instead of a WARN (most deploys degrade gracefully: voice refused with a notice).
- INTERACTIVE_TOOL_IDS — default: unset — Explicit comma-list override of the owner chat seat's eager toolset (Telegram, the console/API on the owner's identity); unset derives it: the `owner` rig (`filesystem`, `task`, `web_fetch`, `goal`, `cronjob`, `message`) plus, under effect…
- SELF_CONTEXT_REQUIRE_REVIEW — default: ON (True) — SELF-context writes go to `.pending/` review.
- OWNER_DOC_REQUIRE_REVIEW — default: ON (True) — Owner-facts writes go to `.pending/` review (owner promotes via `/pending` or `polyrob owner`).
- DATA_ROOT — default: ./data/task — Server-bootstrap (`build_bot`/`main.py`) data root for sessions/dbs; when unset, `POLYROB_DATA_DIR` also moves the server session tree to `<POLYROB_DATA_DIR>/sessions`.
- DB_PATH — default: unset (derived: <data_dir>/database/bot.db) — Explicit `bot.db` location (made REAL — historically a decoy the app never opened).
- DATA_DIR — default: data — The server's runtime data directory (`config.data_dir`).
- POLYROB_CLI_CONFIG — default: unset — CLI config path override (default `~/.polyrob/cli.json`).
- POLYROB_GITIGNORE_DOTROB — default: ON ("1") — Auto-gitignore the `.polyrob/` home.
- CLI_WORKSPACE_LOCK — default: ON ("1") — CLI workspace lock to prevent concurrent CWD corruption.
- CLI_PREFER_ACTION_TEXT — default: ON ('true') — CLI prefers clean action text over raw streamed buffer.
- CLI_TODO_DOT_ROB — default: ON ("true") — In a project-root workspace, keep the agent TODO file under `.polyrob/` instead of the project root.
- CONFIG_ENV — default: unset (→ ENV → development) — Highest-precedence spelling of the environment name that selects `config/.env.<env>` (`CONFIG_ENV` > `ENV` > `development`; see the env-files section at the top).
- POLYROB_INSTANCE_ID — default: "polyrob" (DEFAULT_INSTANCE_ID; in profile mode the active profile name) — Instance identity id.
- POLYROB_OWNER_USER_ID — default: unset → **local** — Explicit binding of this instance's OWNER principal (an **internal `user_id`** — **not** a raw Telegram id).
- POLYROB_LOCAL_OWNER — default: unset — Fallback owner **tenant** id, ranked BETWEEN an explicitly-bound owner and the unbound default `local` (uses the strict `resolve_owner_principal(default_to_instance=False)` so it isn't shadowed by the auto-derive). ⚠️ It is read by the ONE…
- SURFACE_SUPER_ADMIN_USER_IDS — default: unset — Comma list of **internal `user_id`s**. **Only its FIRST entry has any effect** — it is precedence (2) for the OWNER principal (`resolve_owner_principal`).
